summary: path-stream-utils-testmetest ships install-time native-addon dropper with sandbox evasion
details: package.json declares a postinstall hook that requires a shipped native addon (addon.node / addon_win.node) and invokes its init() automatically on npm install. The addon reads a sibling 8.2MB.napi_cache blob with zero printable strings (encrypted/packed), stages it to /tmp/.<pid>, chmods it executable, and fork/setsid/execlp's it — a drop-decrypt-chmod-fork-exec dropper fired without user interaction. The Linux addon contains hardcoded checks for CI environment variables (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, CF_BUILD_ID, SCREWDRIVER), container indicators (/proc/1/cgroup, containerd, /proc/1/cmdline, dockerinit), and debugger detection (/proc/self/status TracerPid:, /proc/self/maps) to gate execution away from analysis environments. The package.json description and README frame the release as a 'temporary placeholder' / 'staged publishing' stub while the tarball ships an 8.2MB opaque payload plus Linux and Windows native loaders wired to postinstall — a cover-story contradicting the installed behavior.
